subject: Architecture
title: The Jeddah Tower: The Unfinished Mile
description: A quick, practical guide to The Jeddah Tower: The Unfinished Mile.

hook.text: Saudi Arabia started building a tower meant to reach one kilometer — 3,281 feet. It stopped at one-third.

buildup.text: The Jeddah Tower was designed by Adrian Smith, the same architect behind the Burj Khalifa.

discovery.text: At a full kilometer, the building would sway noticeably. Tuned mass dampers would keep occupants comfortable.

twist.text: Construction halted in 2018 after the arrest of the project's main backer in a corruption crackdown.

climax.text: The project has restarted and paused multiple times. If completed, it would be 568 feet taller than the Burj.

punchline.text: The tallest building in the world might be the one that's never finished.

quiz.question: Why did construction of the Jeddah Tower halt in 2018?
options: Engineers discovered the foundation soil was unstable
The project backer was arrested in a corruption crackdown
A typhoon destroyed the partially built structure

details.summary: Jeddah Tower in Saudi Arabia was designed to be the first building to reach one kilometer in height. Construction began in 2013 but stalled at roughly one-third completion due to financial and legal disputes. Whether it will ever be finished remains one of architecture's great open questions.
details.whyItMatters: Jeddah Tower tests whether sheer ambition can outrun practical constraints. Its stalled state reveals that building the world's tallest is as much a financial and political challenge as an engineering one.
takeaways: Designed to be the first kilometer-tall building
Construction stalled at roughly one-third completion
Financial and legal disputes halted the project

faq.question: Why did construction on Jeddah Tower stop?
faq.answer: A combination of financial difficulties, legal disputes involving the project's developers, and the broader economic slowdown connected to falling oil prices and the Saudi anti-corruption campaign of 2017 halted work. Construction has been intermittently announced as resuming.

faq.question: Could a one-kilometer building actually be built?
faq.answer: Engineers say yes — the structural challenges are solvable with current technology. The real barriers are financial (extreme cost), logistical (pumping concrete to that height), and practical (elevator travel times, wind pressures). The engineering is ahead of the economics.
